We buy Miami-Dade County houses as-is. Tell us about the property.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Florida statutes and the official Miami-Dade County pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

In Miami-Dade County the clerk of the circuit court is the recorder, and deeds, mortgages and liens are kept in the Official Records. This guide shows where to search them and what Florida law says about recording.

Where to search Miami-Dade County records

  • Miami-Dade Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller is the county recorder.
  • Search deeds, mortgages, liens and other instruments in the Official Records search.
  • Recording fees are on the clerk's fee page.

What the Miami-Dade County clerk's pages state

  • Recording fee for most documents is $10 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page; Lis Pendens $5 first page and $4 each additional page. Copies $1 per page plus $2 certification.
  • E-recording is offered through approved vendors and an eRecording Web Service for Notices of Commencement and Declarations of Domicile; eRecorded documents take approximately 1 to 3 business days to be viewable.

What Florida law says about recording

  • The clerk of the circuit court is the recorder of all instruments the clerk is required or authorized by law to record in the county, and records all instruments in one general series called 'Official Records'. (Fla. Stat. Sec. 28.222(1)-(2)).
  • Instruments recorded in the Official Records must remain open to the public for inspection and copying; the clerk need not perform services without the service charges in s. 28.24. (Fla. Stat. Sec. 28.222(7)).
  • No conveyance, transfer or mortgage of real property (or lease of 1 year or longer) is good against creditors or subsequent purchasers for valuable consideration without notice unless recorded according to law. (Fla. Stat. Sec. 695.01(1)).
  • Recording fee for an instrument not more than 14 inches by 8.5 inches: first page or fraction $5.00; each additional page $4.00 (plus any other charges the clerk imposes; this is the s. 28.24(13) line). (Fla. Stat. Sec. 28.24(13)).
Need to sell a Miami-Dade County house?
We buy Miami-Dade County houses as-is. A title company searches the records at closing.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Installment plan terms
  • Tax deed sale venue (DeedExpress page not opened)
  • Date bills are mailed for real estate (page says payable Nov 1)

Miami-Dade County property records FAQ

Who records deeds in Miami-Dade County, FL?

The clerk of the circuit court is the recorder and keeps the Official Records (Fla. Stat. 28.222).

Are Official Records public?

Yes. Instruments recorded in the Official Records stay open to public inspection and copying.

What is the statewide recording fee?

For an instrument up to 14 by 8.5 inches the statute lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus other charges (Fla. Stat. 28.24). Check the clerk's fee page for the current total.
